explanation: Findings from the Human Genome Project revealed that humans possess approximately 20,500 genes, most of which code for proteins. In a typical human protein-coding gene, roughly 95% of the sequence consists of introns. Large portions of the human genome were historically labeled as 'junk DNA' because they do not specify the amino acid sequence of a polypeptide; however, many of these regions are transcribed into regulatory RNA molecules. Structurally, genes were historically defined as discrete units of heredity located at a specific locus on a chromosome. Eukaryotic gene structure is far more complex than that of prokaryotes (which typically have a single circular chromosome): eukaryotic genes are distributed along the linear chromosome and are fragmented into exons.

questions.q: How does eukaryotic chromosome and gene structure compare to prokaryotes?
opts: Prokaryotes have multiple linear chromosomes, while eukaryotes have one circular chromosome.
Prokaryotes typically possess a single circular chromosome; eukaryotes have genes distributed along complex chromosomes and fragmented into exons.
Prokaryotes have genes fragmented into exons, while eukaryotes have continuous genes with no introns.
Prokaryotic chromosomes are bound by histones, while eukaryotic chromosomes are free.
